about: The inputs of tools/review/measure_fidelity.py for three films of the same script. The tool takes flags, not this file: put each film's files in its folder, then run the command from the repository root. Score each film on the script its narration was generated from, never on a recogniser's transcript; a no-prompt Whisper word list per film only confirms that its audio reads that script. <review> is the comparison folder, <project>/review/YYYY-MM-DD-slug, with one subfolder per film.

flags.--reference: the fixed script: its recording manifest, or the script as plain text
flags.--film NAME=PATH: one per film: the script that film's narration was generated from, in any shape below
flags.--whisper NAME=PATH: optional, one per film: its no-prompt Whisper word list
flags.--out: the result (default fidelity.json): per film its script words, the reference words found in order and fidelity_pct, and with --whisper the words Whisper agrees on and whisper_agree_pct
flags.--diffs: optional: adds the word-level differences, which quote the scripts; keep that output local

scenes.spoken_text_exact: This is sample narration for the first scene.

segments.narration: This is sample narration for the first scene.

text.text: This is sample narration for the first scene.

notes: Make every word list with the same whisper command, model and settings, with word timestamps and no initial prompt, and flatten its segments' words into w, s and e.
Drop the words heard after the last script word (Whisper loops phrases over music and silence), and record what was dropped.

A film with no script of its own cannot be scored this way: say so rather than score its transcript. Scored on recogniser output, one film here came out at 98.4% purely from recogniser errors (research/METHODS.md).
